IN RE: TOM J & RUTH BEINE
PETITION FOR Review for Personal Income Tax
PERIOD(S) 2007-2010
AND NOW, May 20, 2014, pursuant to the Fiscal Code, the Act of 1929, April 9, P.L. 343,
as amended, (72 P.S. § 1 et seq), the Board of Finance and Revenue of the Commonwealth of
Pennsylvania, based upon the reasons set forth herein, hereby ORDERS the following:
Jurisdiction
These petitions come before the Board of Finance and Revenue pursuant to Section
2704 of the Tax Reform Code of 1971, as amended, 72 P.S. § 9704.
Issue
Whether the Petition for Reassessment was timely filed with the Board of Appeals.
Statement of the Case
Petitioners, Tom J. and Ruth Beine, were non-filers were assessed tax, penalties, and
interest for the 2007, 2008, 2009, and 2010 tax years by the Department based on Federal
information. Petitioners were assessed large amounts of tax, penalties, and interest for each
year at issue in assessment notices mailed November 9, 2012.
Petitioners filed appeals at the BOA for all tax years at issue on September 19, 2013,
claiming that the Department had assessed them on gross, instead of net income.
In its Decision and Order dated October 4, 2013, the BOA dismissed the petitions for
being filed 255 days beyond the statutory deadline.
Petitioners file the instant matter at the Board of Finance and Revenue raising the same
arguments as were raised at the BOA. Petitioners were informed of the jurisdictional defect in
a letter dated January 23, 2014. As of this date Petitioners have not provided an explanation
for the late filings at the BOA.
Mailed: TOM J & RUTH BEINE on May 23, 2014

Statement of the Law
Section 340 of the Tax Reform Code of 1971 states in part: “Any taxpayer against
whom an assessment is made may petition the department for a reassessment pursuant to
Article XXVII.” 72 P.S. § 7340.
General rule.--A taxpayer may file a petition for reassessment with the department
within 90 days after the mailing date of the notice of assessment. 72 P.S. § 9702(a).
Our Supreme Court has held that limitations periods are absolute conditions to a right to
obtain relief. Federal Deposits Ins. Corp. v. Board of Finance and Revenue, 368 Pa. 463, 469-
470; 84 A.2d 495, 498-499 (1951). In any case, equitable principles cannot vary the statutory
time requirements. See Bethlehem Steel Co. v. Board of Finance and Revenue, 431 Pa. 1,
10; 244 A.2d 767, 772 (1968) and Cooper v. Commonwealth, 700 A.2d 553, 554-555 (Pa.
Commw. 1997).
Conclusion
Petitioners filed the Petitions for Reassessment at the Board of Appeals beyond the
ninety day filing period. Petitioners failed to provide evidence to overcome the jurisdiction
issue. Therefore, the Board of Appeals properly dismissed Petitioner’s claims for failure to file
a timely appeal of the assessment. See 72 P.S. § 9702(a).
Accordingly, this Board enters the following:
ORDER
These petitions are dismissed.
